doc.title: Loren Schoenberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019

chapter: Benny Goodman and the big band
title: Goodman hires the band for the 1985 anniversary and fires Schoenberg
summary: Goodman refuses a reunion band for PBS, hires Schoenberg's band, then replaces him with Ted Nash.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: he had a Mercedes. So on some weekends I would actually drive Benny up with Carol to their house, like the chauffeur, drive them up to Stamford, leave them, then I would drive his car back and park it in his garage. And I mean I had never driven a Mercedes Benz but that’s another story. Drive it back, park it in his garage, and somehow they would get back on Sunday. Well one time I went up there and one time I went up there and he invited me for lunch and one time he said let’s go swimming, he had a swimming pool. Okay you know so we went swimming. And while we were swimming he told me that he was going to hire my band. Because what happened was Dick Hyman had been approached by public television because it was the Fiftieth Anniversary of Benny’s breakthrough, 1985. And they wanted to do a public television show. So Dick Hyman was going to put together a band of Jimmy Maxwell and all the guys, Hymie Shertzer , Toots Mondello, and all the guys that were still alive, and all the great musicians, and frankly Benny didn’t want to see them anymore. And I don’t think they really wanted to see him. It was not a warm relationship between those people unfortunately, for the most part. Some loved him but most didn’t. And so he told Dick Hyman and PBS, “I’m not going to do it with a reunion band.” Then he heard my band and he wound up hiring my band and we became the last Benny Goodman Orchestra. So he started rehearsing it and changing, and that’s a whole nother story. I don’t know how much you want to get into it. But that was a whole thing seeing him rehearse Fletcher Henderson and all those arrangements. Got rid of Mel Lewis, didn’t want Mel Lewis so we had Louie Bellson. He wanted Bob Haggart on bass. So we put Bob Haggart and Louie Bellson in the band, and Dick Hyman took the place of Dick Katz. But outside of that I mean it was the same band that I had had. And boy was it a lesson for me, seeing what a great band leader can do to what was a very good band, and then turn it into the sparkling, shining Benny Goodman Orchestra. And then I joined the great legion of people who were let go of a Benny Goodman band. My own band.
